title: Known-truth blocked-randomized causal repair-effect estimation

owns: randomized trial eligibility and assignment contract
deterministic measurement-error bound and robust effect interval

paradigm.restoration_vs_effect: A matched pre/post result in #5094 establishes observed restoration within a declared envelope. It does not estimate what would have happened under a different intervention.
paradigm.randomized_reference: P0 uses known-truth blocked randomized synthetic or controlled test-bench cases so assignment is independent of potential outcomes by design.
paradigm.observational_boundary: This v0.1 estimator rejects observational assignment. Target-trial emulation, longitudinal g-methods and sensitivity bounds require separate assumptions and benchmark versions.
paradigm.oracle_separation: Potential outcomes live in a separate scoring object. The estimator function receives only the randomized trial and observed outcomes; it cannot use the oracle to estimate the treatment effect.
paradigm.measurement_uncertainty: The sampling standard error describes randomization/sampling uncertainty. A separately declared deterministic absolute measurement-error bound is computed from calibrated per-unit bounds and expands a robust effect interval; it is not mislabelled as a standard error or assumed independent.

estimand.name: finite_population_average_treatment_effect
estimand.formula: mean_i(Y_i(treatment) - Y_i(control)) over the eligible randomized units
estimand.unit: declared outcome unit and metric; never a blended health score
estimand.allocation: blocked randomization with frozen treatment/control counts within each predeclared stratum
estimand.weighting: stratum difference in means weighted by the stratum share of randomized units

estimator.variance: Neyman conservative variance from within-arm sample variances; unidentifiable finite-population treatment-effect variance is not subtracted Deterministic measurement-error bounds are not inserted into the Neyman sampling variance; they are reported separately and expand a robust interval.
estimator.interval: normal-approximation interval at predeclared 90%, 95% or 99% confidence level; coverage requires adequate sample size and randomization assumptions
estimator.test: two-sided exact Fisher randomization test under the sharp null, conditional on fixed treatment counts per stratum
estimator.baseline: pre-assignment baselines are checked for time availability but are not adjusted in v0.1
estimator.reporting: raw treatment-minus-control effect plus a sign-reoriented value whose positive direction means benefit under the declared outcome direction

measurement_provenance.baseline: Baseline and outcome records carry evidence digest, source ID, measurement principle, dependency domain, quality state, calibration record digest and calibration validity-until time.
measurement_provenance.outcome_method: The measurement principle is frozen at trial level and every outcome record must match it.
measurement_provenance.quality: Only valid measurement quality and verified calibration that remains valid through evidence availability are accepted.
measurement_provenance.uncertainty: Each outcome measurement carries a deterministic absolute-error bound. The contrast bound is the stratum-weighted sum of treatment-arm and control-arm mean absolute-error bounds.
measurement_provenance.reporting: The reported Neyman standard error and normal-approximation sampling interval remain sampling-only. A second robust interval expands the sampling interval by the deterministic measurement-error bound.
measurement_provenance.baseline_use: Baseline provenance is validated, but baseline covariates remain unused by the P0 estimator.

hard_gates: Only blocked randomized assignment is accepted by this P0 estimator.
Assignment plan digest and assignment audit reference must be present and frozen before assignment.
Every independent randomization unit appears exactly once; rows/windows are not independent units.
Every unit belongs to one declared stratum.
Each stratum has at least two planned treatment and two planned control units.
Observed treatment/control counts must exactly match the frozen stratum allocation.
No stratum may omit a randomized arm; no extrapolation across positivity failure.
Assignment evidence must be available no later than assignment time.
Baseline evidence must be observed and available before assignment.
Post-intervention outcome must be observed no earlier than the preregistered follow-up horizon.
Outcome evidence must be available by the analysis as-of time.
Outcome metric and units must match the preregistered trial contract.
Every assignment, baseline and outcome record must carry a valid evidence digest.
No post-assignment or future maintenance record may enter baseline eligibility.
Potential-outcome oracle is not accepted by the estimator and is used only by the synthetic scoring function.
The oracle must bind the exact unit set and agree with each unit's observed assigned potential outcome.
Exact randomization enumeration is bounded to 16 independent units; larger experiments fail closed in v0.1.
Confidence intervals state their Neyman variance and normal-approximation method.
Outcome direction is explicit; raw effect and benefit-oriented effect are both reported.
The report always denies maintenance authorization, physical restoration authority and operating-restriction clearance.
Baseline and outcome measurement records bind a non-empty source identifier, measurement principle and dependency domain.
Baseline and outcome measurement quality must be valid; missing, stale, rejected or conflicted records are not accepted.
Baseline and outcome records bind a calibration-record SHA-256 and verified calibration status.
Calibration validity must extend through the time the corresponding measurement became available.
The outcome measurement principle is frozen in the trial and every unit outcome must use that declared principle.
Each baseline and outcome measurement carries a finite non-negative deterministic absolute-error bound.
The estimator reports the Neyman sampling standard error separately from the measurement-error bound.
The effect uncertainty report includes a robust interval formed by expanding the sampling interval by the deterministic weighted measurement-error bound.
The synthetic oracle consistency check also binds the measurement-error bound and robust interval.
nonclaims: Randomization metadata and hashes do not authenticate the allocation issuer.
Passing synthetic known-truth tests does not identify effects in observational maintenance records.
No RUL, recurrence hazard or long-term durability effect is estimated.
No causal effect is inferred from a before/after difference alone.
No maintenance policy or work authorization is produced.

comparators.description: Before/after mean difference without a counterfactual assignment design.
Stratified difference in means with known blocked allocation.
Finite-population effect calculated from hidden paired potential outcomes; never an estimator input.

research_targets_not_achieved.target: Absolute ATE bias below 5% of declared outcome scale on adequately sampled known-truth blocked trials
85–95% empirical coverage for nominal 90% intervals on adequately sampled held-out randomized cases
Zero accepted causal effect for nonrandomized or positivity-failing P0 inputs
100% of estimates unchanged when only the separate potential-outcome oracle changes
Zero maintenance, physical-restoration or operating-clearance side effects

claim_ceiling: This P0 module estimates a finite-population average effect only for the declared blocked randomized experiment and observed follow-up outcome. It does not establish observational identification, marine-engine repair effectiveness, durability, RUL, vessel safety, maintenance authority or permission to operate. Calibration/source digests and the declared absolute-error bounds are structurally checked metadata; this module does not authenticate issuers, prove calibration traceability or establish that the stated deterministic error bounds are physically valid.
